source_text: Sors non fortuna caeca; providentia Dei. Sortes apostolicae. Dominus disponit.
thought_title: The lot is God's providence, not blind chance
orientation: Origen is explaining the meaning of the lot in the Levitical rite, after discussing how baptism sends sins into the desert.
pass_a_gloss: Lot [is] not fortune blind; providence of God. Lots apostolic. [The] Lord arranges.

choices.english: The lot is not blind chance
choices.why: Keeps the noun 'lot' as the subject and renders 'fortuna caeca' as 'blind chance' to preserve the contrast between the lot and random fortune.
rejected: The lot is not blind fortune
A lot is not blind luck

choices.why: Uses the standard English theological term 'providence' for 'providentia' and keeps the genitive 'of God' explicit.
Preserves the plural 'sortes' and the adjective 'apostolicae' as a predicate, matching the terse Latin style.
Keeps 'Dominus' as subject and 'disponit' as present tense verb, preserving the active role of the Lord in arranging the lot.

pass_b_english: The lot is not blind chance; it is the providence of God. The lots are apostolic. The Lord disposes.
